cues.en: Can I tell you something I'm bad at?
cues.zh: 我能跟你说说我不擅长的事吗？

cues.en: I am terrible at making clickbait.
cues.zh: 我做标题党烂透了。

cues.en: Up until two years ago, my most popular video was about a basketball being dropped from a dam with a bit of backspin.
cues.zh: 直到两年前，我最火的视频还是关于一个篮球从大坝上掉下来、带点回旋的那种。

cues.en: It takes off like a rocket and shoots out way further than you'd expect.
cues.zh: 它像火箭一样飞出去，飞得比你想的远多了。

cues.en: This video was embedded on literally hundreds of news websites, and in its first week, it got 16,300,000
cues.zh: 这个视频被嵌入了 literally 数百个新闻网站，第一周就获得了1630万

cues.en: views.
cues.zh: 次观看。

cues.en: But almost none of those views came on the YouTube platform.
cues.zh: 但几乎所有这些观看都不是在YouTube平台上。

cues.en: Why? Because I gave it this thumbnail
cues.zh: 为什么？因为我给它配了这个缩略图

cues.en: and I called it strange applications
cues.zh: 而且我把它叫做马格努斯效应的

cues.en: of the Magnus effect. This
cues.zh: 奇怪应用。这个

cues.en: video is sponsored by KiwiCo. More about them at the end of the show. Now, I believe within YouTube, I'm used as an example of how not to package your video. As if to demonstrate just how bad a title and thumbnail this is, someone else re uploaded the video with a clever title, Basketball Dropped From Damn.
cues.zh: 视频由KiwiCo赞助。节目最后会详细介绍他们。现在，我相信在YouTube内部，我被当作如何不包装你视频的反面教材。就好像为了展示标题和缩略图有多糟糕，有人重新上传了视频，配了个聪明的标题，篮球从大坝掉落。

cues.en: And within a few weeks, that video had received tens of millions of views on YouTube. This is when YouTube gave me access to Content ID. That's the system that allows you to earn revenue when someone else reuploads your videos,
cues.zh: 几周内，那个视频在YouTube上就获得了几千万次观看。这时YouTube给了我Content ID的访问权限。那是个让你在别人重新上传你的视频时赚取收入的系统，

cues.en: which was good, but I still wasn't very good at clickbait.
cues.zh: 这很好，但我还是不太擅长做标题党。

cues.en: So for this video, I called in an expert.
cues.zh: 所以为了这个视频，我请来了一位专家。

cues.en: I wanted to see your reaction face. Can you give me like a reaction face? Like, what's a good thumbnail face? Oh, I got you. This is a thumbnail face.
cues.zh: 我想看你的反应脸。你能给我个反应脸吗？比如，什么才是好的缩略图脸？哦，我懂你。这就是缩略图脸。

cues.en: I I have like 10 I go through the motions of, like,
cues.zh: 我拍了大概十来张，摆摆各种姿势，

cues.en: we and just take the best one. I probably have like 500 of these just saved and we could just photoshop my face on my face. Then I don't really have to do it anymore.
cues.zh: 然后挑出最好的一张。我电脑里大概存了五百张这种照片，完全可以把脸 P 到自己身上，以后就不用每次都重新拍了。

cues.en: When I started on this platform some ten years ago, clickbait was less important.
cues.zh: 大约十年前我刚入驻这个平台时，“标题党”还没那么重要。

cues.en: Subscribers were what mattered because most of the views came from the sub feed and videos went viral usually by getting a lot of attention elsewhere like on Reddit or Facebook,
cues.zh: 那时最关键的是订阅数，因为大部分播放量都来自订阅信息流，视频走红通常是因为在 Reddit 或 Facebook 等其他平台上引起了广泛关注，

cues.en: not due to the YouTube algorithm.
cues.zh: 而不是靠 YouTube 的算法。

cues.en: But once you had a big video and people subscribed,
cues.zh: 但一旦你出了一期爆款视频，吸引了大家订阅，

cues.en: well, then your next video would likely get a lot of views from those subscribers. So YouTube would take that popular video and share it with more people, and so you get more subscribers in a positive feedback loop.
cues.zh: 你的下一个视频就很可能会从这些订阅者那里获得大量播放。于是 YouTube 会把这个热门视频推荐给更多人，形成正向反馈循环，让你收获更多订阅。

cues.en: But soon YouTube realized that this did not create the best experience for the viewer. They discovered that showing people only videos from channels they were subscribed to led to fewer clicks,
cues.zh: 但很快 YouTube 就意识到，这种模式并没有为观众带来最佳体验。他们发现，只向用户推荐已订阅频道的视频，反而会导致点击量减少、

cues.en: less watch time, and less engagement with the site as a whole. Plus, they knew that relying on other platforms to drive traffic to viral hits was risky since those other platforms might disable the traffic at any time.
cues.zh: 观看时长缩短，以及全站的用户互动率下降。此外他们也清楚，靠其他平台引流来打造爆款风险太高，因为那些平台随时可能切断流量来源。

cues.en: So they needed to make YouTube a destination in itself.
cues.zh: 所以他们必须把 YouTube 自身打造成一个目的地。

cues.en: They wanted people to come to YouTube,
cues.zh: 他们希望用户主动来到 YouTube，

cues.en: see videos that interested them, click on at least one of them, and watch it for a while. Ideally, get sucked down the YouTube rabbit hole and spend hours on the site without even noticing it. The ultimate resource is people's time and attention, and every platform is trying to capture as much of it as possible.
cues.zh: 看到感兴趣的内容，至少点开一个看上一会儿。最理想的情况是，彻底沦陷在 YouTube 的无限信息流中，不知不觉就刷上几个小时。毕竟终极资源就是用户的时间和注意力，而每个平台都在竭尽全力争夺它们。

cues.en: So to make YouTube this go to destination,
cues.zh: 所以为了让YouTube成为首选目的地，

cues.en: they had to decrease the importance of subscribers,
cues.zh: 他们不得不降低订阅者的重要性，

cues.en: make it less like a podcast app where you only get the shows you're subscribed to, and more like Reddit where stuff with the most engagement rises to the top. But that necessarily meant increasing the importance of clickbait.
cues.zh: 让它不再像播客应用那样只能看到你订阅的节目，而更像Reddit那样让互动最多内容浮到顶部。但这必然意味着提升标题党的地位。

cues.en: Now, there seems to be a paradox when it comes to clickbait. People almost universally
cues.zh: 说到标题党，似乎存在一个悖论。人们几乎普遍

cues.en: claim to hate it,
cues.zh: 声称讨厌它，

cues.en: but you also see it everywhere.
cues.zh: 但你到处都能看到它。

cues.en: So why is this? Well, one of the problems is we don't all agree on the definition of clickbait. When I Google it, the top definition is on the internet content whose main purpose is to attract attention and encourage visitors to click on a link to a particular web page. We could call this type one clickbait
cues.zh: 那为什么会这样？问题之一是我们对标题党的定义并不一致。我在谷歌上搜，最热门的定义是：互联网内容，其主要目的是吸引注意力、鼓励访客点击指向特定网页的链接。我们可以把这称为第一类标题党

cues.en: and there doesn't seem to be anything wrong with it. I mean, if you didn't try to attract attention and get people to click on your links then you wouldn't really be doing your job. But there is a second definition,
cues.zh: 而且这似乎没什么问题。我的意思是，如果你不试着吸引注意力、让人们点击你的链接，那你就没在干好本职工作。但还有第二种定义，

cues.en: one that I think more people ascribe to, which is something such as a headline designed to make readers want to click on a hyperlink, especially when the link leads to content of dubious value or interest.
cues.zh: 我认为更多人认同这一种：比如旨在让读者想点击超链接的标题，尤其是当链接指向价值或趣味存疑的内容时。

cues.en: Wikipedia
cues.zh: 维基百科

cues.en: says a defining characteristic of clickbait is that it is sensationalized
cues.zh: 说标题党的一个决定性特征是耸人听闻

cues.en: or misleading,
cues.zh: 或具有误导性，

cues.en: and it also talks about teasers that intentionally withhold information to exploit the curiosity gap. They give you enough information to make you curious,
cues.zh: 它还谈到故意隐瞒信息以利用好奇心缺口的悬念式内容。它们给你足够的信息让你好奇，

cues.en: but not enough to satisfy that curiosity.
cues.zh: 但又不足以满足那份好奇心。

cues.en: Here are two actual titles from a news website.
cues.zh: 以下是新闻网站上的两个真实标题。

cues.en: Nine out of 10 Americans are completely wrong about this mind blowing fact,
cues.zh: 90%的美国人对这个令人震惊的事实完全搞错了，

cues.en: and someone gave some kids some scissors.
cues.zh: 还有人给了几个孩子一些剪刀。

cues.en: Here's what happened next.
cues.zh: 接下来发生的事是这样的。

cues.en: I think we can all agree that these are examples of bad type two clickbait.
cues.zh: 我想我们都同意，这些是糟糕的第二类标题党的例子。

cues.en: Now imagine a clickbait space where on one axis you have how misleading or sensationalized it is and on the other how much information is intentionally withheld to create a curiosity gap. Well then these two titles fall in the top right corner
cues.zh: 现在想象一个标题党空间，一个轴表示它有多误导或多耸人听闻，另一个轴表示它故意隐瞒了多少信息来制造好奇缺口。那么这两个标题就落在右上角

cues.en: and these are the zones of type two clickbait.
cues.zh: 这些就是第二类标题党的区域。

cues.en: At the other extreme, you have things that are so unsensationalized
cues.zh: 在另一个极端，有些东西完全不耸人听闻，

cues.en: as to be dull.
cues.zh: 以至于枯燥乏味。

cues.en: You could call this the dead zone.
cues.zh: 你可以把这叫做死区。

cues.en: Now, here is where you would find strange applications of the Magnus effect. I mean, I didn't tell you what the applications were.
cues.zh: 现在，这里是你找到马格努斯效应奇怪应用的地方。我是说，我没告诉你这些应用是什么。

cues.en: Now in the middle is where you would find type one clickbait.
cues.zh: 中间则是你找到第一类标题党的地方。

cues.en: But honestly, I think type one and type two clickbait are so different that we shouldn't even use the same word for them. Instead of type one clickbait, my friend and YouTuber Brady Haran suggested
cues.zh: 但老实说，我觉得第一类和第二类标题党差别太大，我们甚至不该用同一个词来称呼它们。我的朋友、YouTuber Brady Haran 建议，不用第一类标题党，

cues.en: legit bait. I mean, it might sound enticing, but it is legit.
cues.zh: 而叫合法诱饵。我是说，它可能听起来很诱人，但它是合法的。

cues.en: Instead of type two clickbait, we could use click trap, click trick,
cues.zh: 不用第二类标题党，我们可以用点击陷阱、点击花招、

cues.en: link trap, or dupe shoot.
cues.zh: 链接陷阱，或者诱骗点击。

cues.en: What's important to recognize is that for any given video, there is no one true title and thumbnail.
cues.zh: 重要的是要认识到，对于任何一个视频，都没有唯一正确的标题和缩略图。

cues.en: Each video could have hundreds or thousands of different legit bait titles. For example, how does a zero g plane work? I went on a plane that does parabolic trajectories.
cues.zh: 每个视频都可能有成百上千个不同的正当诱饵式标题。比如，零重力飞机是怎么运作的？我上了一架做抛物线飞行的飞机。

cues.en: What happens to fire on a zero g plane?
cues.zh: 在零重力飞机上，火会发生什么？

cues.en: Now, the most enticing titles and thumbnails are found close to type two clickbait.
cues.zh: 现在，最吸引人的标题和缩略图都接近第二类标题党。

cues.en: I'm reminded of the infographic by Smarter Every Day showing that on social media, the greatest engagement occurs close to the boundary of what's allowable.
cues.zh: 这让我想起Smarter Every Day的一张信息图，它表明在社交媒体上，最高的互动量出现在可允许范围的边界附近。

cues.en: But remember that everyone's definition of clickbait is different, and everyone's perceptions of words and images are different. So these are not clear boundaries. They're actually kind of fuzzy.
cues.zh: 但请记住，每个人对标题党的定义都不同，每个人对文字和图像的感知也不同。所以这些并不是清晰的边界。它们其实是有点模糊的。

cues.en: What for one person might be a legit bait, for someone else could be a click trap.
cues.zh: 对一个人来说可能是正当诱饵，对另一个人来说就可能是点击陷阱。

cues.en: What's clear is that on a site where click through rate is important, clickbait of all types is inevitable. How important to a video success is the title and thumbnail? Very important. Of course. If they don't click on the video, they don't watch it. You can't get 10,000,000 views unless 10,000,000 people click on the video. So, I mean, it's literally that simple. They don't click on it. They don't watch it. So why is clickbait everywhere?
cues.zh: 明确的是，在一个点击率很重要的网站上，各种类型的标题党都不可避免。标题和缩略图对视频成功有多重要？非常重要。当然。如果他们不点击视频，他们就不会观看。除非有1000万人点击视频，否则你不可能获得1000万次观看。所以，我的意思是， literally就是这么简单。他们不点击，他们就不观看。那么，为什么标题党无处不在？

cues.en: Well, because it works.
cues.zh: 嗯，因为它有效。

cues.en: More enticing thumbnails get more clicks despite some people's claims that they won't click or they'll unsub.
cues.zh: 更吸引人的缩略图会获得更多点击，尽管有些人声称他们不会点击，或者他们会取消订阅。

cues.en: It's just like evolution.
cues.zh: 这就像生物演化一样。

cues.en: Whatever survives multiplies and traits become amplified.
cues.zh: 能存活下来的就会繁衍，其特征也会不断被放大。

cues.en: If you don't begrudge the giraffe its long neck so it can reach the highest leaves, can you begrudge a YouTuber the big red arrow that allows them to reach further audiences?
cues.zh: 如果你不怪长颈鹿为了吃到最高的树叶而长出长脖子，那你又怎么能怪 YouTuber 用大大的红箭头来吸引更多观众呢？

cues.en: I talked about this in my video two years ago. To be successful as a YouTuber, need to optimize two things, watch time and the click through rate of your videos. That's the number of times the title and thumbnail are clicked divided by the total number of times they're shown. That's the number of impressions.
cues.zh: 我两年前在视频里就聊过这个。作为一名 YouTuber，要想成功必须优化两点：观看时长，以及视频的点击率。点击率就是标题和缩略图的点击次数除以总展示次数，也就是曝光量。

cues.en: Now at the time, this was something of a revelation for me because I always thought my job was to make great videos and then a title and thumbnail that adequately represented what the video was about. But now I've realized that making the title and thumbnail is at least half the job.
cues.zh: 当时这对我来说算是个巨大的启发，因为我以前总以为自己的职责就是做好视频，然后配上一个如实反映内容的标题和缩略图。但现在我意识到，做标题和缩略图至少占了一半的工作量。

cues.en: This is not just because better titles and thumbnails get you more clicks, but because better titles and thumbnails will get you way more impressions.
cues.zh: 这不仅是因为更好的标题和缩略图能带来更多点击，更因为它们能让你获得多得多的曝光量。

cues.en: YouTube has limited real estate with which to show you virtually infinite content
cues.zh: YouTube 能够用来展示内容的版面极其有限，而内容本身却几乎是无穷无尽的，

cues.en: and so it's not enough to make a good video even if people watch all of it. You also have to make a title and thumbnail that gets clicked especially in competition with other really good titles and thumbnails. That's the only way you can expect YouTube to give you more impressions.
cues.zh: 所以光做好视频是不够的，哪怕观众全都看完了也不行。你还得做出能吸引点击的标题和缩略图，尤其是在跟其他同样优秀的标题和缩略图竞争时。只有这样，你才能指望 YouTube 给你分配更多曝光。

cues.en: Now, the big development since my last video on this is YouTube introduced real time metrics like views, impressions, and click through rate. Now, I suggested this would create an arms race. So what you can bet will happen is that creators will launch a video and then they'll be sitting there with all these different variants of thumbnails and they'll be swapping them out and looking at what that does to click through rate and then going with the one that leads to the greatest click through rate. And this is basically what has happened. Let me give you my favorite example.
cues.zh: 自从我上一个相关视频之后，最大的进展是 YouTube 推出了实时指标，比如播放量、展示量和点击率。我当时就说过，这会引发一场军备竞赛。所以可以打赌会发生的是：创作者发布视频后，会守着各种不同版本的缩略图，不停替换，观察对点击率的影响，最后选点击率最高的那个。这基本就是后来发生的事。我给你们举个我最喜欢的例子。

cues.en: Last year, I made a video about asteroids
cues.zh: 去年，我做过一个关于小行星的视频

cues.en: which I thought was really good. I called it asteroids, Earth's biggest threat which is something Stephen Hawking said and people were very positive about the video. They thought it was maybe one of my best, but the performance was well below average. In its first day, Asteroids was ranked ninth out of my previous 10 videos.
cues.zh: 我觉得那个视频很不错。我给它起名《小行星：地球最大的威胁》，这是 Stephen Hawking 说过的一句话。大家对视频反响很积极，觉得可能是我最好的作品之一，但表现却远低于平均水平。发布第一天，《小行星》在我之前 10 个视频里排第九。

cues.en: It was probably on target for about one and a half million views.
cues.zh: 它大概有望达到 150 万播放量。

cues.en: So I tried different titles and thumbnails like asteroid impact, what are our chances or asteroid impact, what could we do? But none of these changes got much traction.
cues.zh: 所以我试了不同的标题和缩略图，比如《小行星撞击，我们有多大几率？》或者《小行星撞击，我们能做什么？》。但这些改动都没什么效果。

cues.en: And then on day three after launch, I changed the title and thumbnail to These Are the Asteroids to Worry About. And immediately,
cues.zh: 然后发布第三天，我把标题和缩略图改成了《这些才是该担心的小行星》。紧接着，

cues.en: the video started doing better. It quickly shot up from almost my worst performing video to my best.
cues.zh: 视频表现开始变好。它很快从几乎是我表现最差的视频，蹿升成了我表现最好的视频。

cues.en: It now has 14,000,000
cues.zh: 现在它有 1400 万

cues.en: views.
cues.zh: 次观看。

cues.en: Nothing about the video changed, just that one image and 38 characters.
cues.zh: 视频本身没有任何变化，只是换了一张图和 38 个字符。

cues.en: But because of that, the video has reached nearly 10 times as many people as it otherwise would have. And the title and thumbnail accurately describe what the video is about. I mean, sure, there's a curiosity gap, but you couldn't explain the whole concept in the length of the title.
cues.zh: 但正因如此，这个视频触达的人数几乎是不改时的 10 倍。而且标题和缩略图准确描述了视频内容。当然，这里确实有悬念，但标题那么短，根本没法把整个概念讲清楚。

cues.en: So if you see a YouTuber changing titles and thumbnails, this is why.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你看到 YouTuber 在改标题和缩略图，原因就在这。

cues.en: Because that effort can be rewarded many times over. I've seen people objecting to this practice because they think the creator is trying to dupe their audience, get them to click on the same video more than once, but that's not it. The whole point is to get YouTube to show the title and thumbnail to more people. We're trying to increase
cues.zh: 因为这份努力能获得成倍的回报。我见过有人反对这种做法，觉得创作者是想骗观众，让他们把同一个视频点开不止一次，但并不是这样。重点是要让 YouTube 把标题和缩略图展示给更多人。我们想增加

cues.en: the number of impressions, which is heavily dependent on the click through rate. Now, lot of my recent videos have this typical view curve. There's an initial spike after I release the video and then a dip, and then a second bump after I have figured out a better title and thumbnail.
cues.zh: 展示次数，而这在很大程度上取决于点击率。我最近很多视频都有这种典型的播放曲线。发布后会先有一个高峰，然后回落，等我找到更好的标题和缩略图后，又会出现第二个小高峰。

cues.en: I changed the title and thumbnail and I watched the real time view graph. What I'm looking for is a noticeable bump in views.
cues.zh: 我改了标题和缩略图，然后盯着实时播放量图表。我要找的就是播放量明显上涨。

cues.en: Sometimes there's no change,
cues.zh: 有时毫无变化，

cues.en: sometimes it gets worse, but on occasions when you see something like this, well then you know you've found a winner.
cues.zh: 有时还会变差，但偶尔你看到这样的曲线，那你就知道，自己找到赢家了。

cues.en: This is something all the big YouTubers are doing. Not even mister beast knows exactly which thumbnail will work best beforehand. Have you ever changed the title and thumbnail and then the video did better? Oh, of course. So every video, I usually make, like, two or three thumbnails. And then if it's not doing as well as I want, we usually just swap them out and see if it does better.
cues.zh: 所有头部 YouTuber 都在这么做。就连 mister beast 事先也无法确知哪个缩略图效果最好。“你试过改完标题和缩略图后，视频数据就变好了吗？”“哦，当然。所以每期视频我通常会做两三个缩略图。如果数据不及预期，我们就会直接换掉，看看表现会不会更好。”

cues.en: Because the thing is, like, you don't really know. I I mean, you could know if you just were an almighty
cues.zh: 因为事实就是，你根本没办法提前知道。我是说，除非你是某种全知全能的……

cues.en: being that could just predict what people would be interested in. But us, you know, usually... Like, you do hide and seek. You don't really know if, like, you hiding in a tree and then someone walking below you is a good thumbnail or if you hiding in a trash can and then walking in front So, you know, just do both and then see which one interests people a little bit more. I feel the same way. But I I do feel like you have a better sense of this than like most people. Of course. I mean, no one gets 40,000,000 views a video. But
cues.zh: 存在，能直接预知大家会对什么感兴趣。但对我们常人来说……比如你做捉迷藏视频，你根本没法确定，是你躲在树上、底下有人走过的画面做缩略图更好，还是你躲在垃圾桶里、有人从面前走过更好。所以干脆两个都做，看看哪个更能吸引人。我也有同感。不过我确实觉得你在这方面的嗅觉比大多数人都要敏锐。当然，毕竟没人能随随便便单支视频拿下 4000 万播放。但是……

cues.en: what is the point in getting more views? If you're cynical, you might say it's all about money and fame. And while there are certainly financial incentives to getting more views, that's not why I do it. As an educational YouTuber, I think there are two very good reasons for using excellent type one clickbait over more straightforward packaging.
cues.zh: 追求更多播放量的意义究竟何在？如果你想法现实甚至悲观一点，可能会说这全是为了名和利。虽然更高的播放量确实能带来经济收益，但这绝不是我这么做的初衷。作为一名教育类 YouTuber，我认为相比平铺直叙的包装，采用优质的第一类“标题党”手法有两个非常充分的理由。

cues.en: To understand the first reason, let's consider two different possible titles for my most recent video. I called it the simplest math problem no one can solve, but it's a video about the Collatz conjecture. So perhaps a more straightforward title would have been simply to call it that.
cues.zh: 为了理解第一个原因，我们来看看我最近那期视频的两个备选标题。我把它叫做《无人能解的最简数学难题》，但视频讲的其实是 Collatz 猜想。所以也许更直接的做法，就是干脆叫这个名字。

cues.en: The problem is if I publish a video called the Collatz conjecture, the most likely people to click on it are those who already know what the Collatz conjecture is. And the vast majority of people will never have heard of it. So for them, the title is meaningless
cues.zh: 问题在于，如果我发一个标题叫《Collatz 猜想》的视频，最可能点进来的，只有那些本来就知道它的人。而绝大多数人根本听都没听过。对他们来说，这个标题毫无意义，

cues.en: and only the very curious or those who really like Veritasium would click.
cues.zh: 只有极度好奇的人，或者 Veritasium 的铁粉才会点进来。

cues.en: In contrast, calling it the simplest math problem no one can solve conveys more information about the video to everyone. And this means more people can click on it, most of whom will never have heard of the Collatz conjecture, so I get to teach them something new.
cues.zh: 相比之下，把它叫做《无人能解的最简数学难题》，能向所有人传递更多关于视频的信息。这意味着会有更多人点击，而他们大多数人都没听说过 Collatz 猜想，这样我就可以教会他们一些新东西。

cues.en: And since the video has a higher click through rate, YouTube shows it to even more people.
cues.zh: 而且由于视频的点击率更高，YouTube 就会把它推荐给更多的人。

cues.en: So if my aim is to increase the level of knowledge in the world by the maximum amount possible,
cues.zh: 所以，如果我的目标是尽可能最大化地提升大众的认知水平，

cues.en: this is the way to do it.
cues.zh: 这才是正确的做法。

cues.en: The second reason we need to optimize titles and thumbnails is to support the major goal of this channel. We are trying to make the best science films on every topic we tackle.
cues.zh: 我们需要优化标题和缩略图的第二个原因，是为了支撑这个频道的首要目标。我们力求在涉足的每一个主题上，都做出最好的科普影片。

cues.en: That means traveling to meet experts and film experiments, hiring people to build props, make spectacular
cues.zh: 这意味着要奔波各地拜访专家并拍摄实验，雇人制作道具，打造精美的

cues.en: animations,
cues.zh: 动画，

cues.en: research, and fact check. We hire expert consultants to double and triple check our work.
cues.zh: 做深入调研和事实核查。我们甚至会聘请专家顾问对我们的内容反复把关。

cues.en: I don't want to make vlogs. I want to make science documentaries on YouTube that put broadcast to shame. And to make this possible and sustainable,
cues.zh: 我不想做视频日志。我想在YouTube上做科学纪录片，让广播电视相形见绌。而要让这件事可行且可持续，

cues.en: the videos have to get views and lots of them. And to do that, we have to make the best titles and thumbnails we can.
cues.zh: 视频就必须获得观看量，而且要很多。为此，我们得尽可能做出最好的标题和缩略图。

cues.en: YouTuber and Patreon CEO, Jack Conte has talked about adjusting your packaging. The idea is know what you're passionate about, what you won't compromise on and that stuff goes in the box. All the rest like what paper it's wrapped in, that's the packaging. So the video is my focus and the title and thumbnail are the packaging that I'm happy to adjust so I can make the type of videos that are important to me. Now, is it ironic that a channel whose whole purpose is to promote a truth seeking mindset has to experiment at the edge of what is truthful in order to fulfill that purpose?
cues.zh: YouTuber兼Patreon CEO Jack Conte谈过调整你的“包装”。理念是清楚你热爱什么、你绝不让步的是什么，这些放进盒子里。其余的一切，比如用什么纸包起来，那就是包装。所以视频是我的重点，标题和缩略图是我乐意调整的包装，这样我才能做出对我重要的那类视频。那么，一个以推广求真心态为宗旨的频道，却不得不在真实性的边缘做实验来实现这个目的，这讽刺吗？

cues.en: It is something that I often worry about. You know, when I did like risk in my life to
cues.zh: 这是我经常担心的事。你知道，当我以前在生活中冒险去做

cues.en: do x, it's like, well, what probability of death does there have to be for you to risk your life? Like, 50%?...
cues.zh: 某事时，就会想，得有多大的死亡概率，你才愿意拿命去冒险？比如50%？……

cues.en: He always overthinks things.
cues.zh: 他总是想太多。

cues.en: He's like, is my life risk enough where I can put I risk my life? You know, I only had a nine percent chance of dying and I need at least a thirteen percent chance. He is so funny. He was the same way two years ago when he asked me all this stuff. I was like, dude, just do whatever makes the most sense. Yeah. I mean, obviously, like, I feel like my instincts are not good. But what I realized is that I don't have to trust my instincts.
cues.zh: 他会想，我的生命风险够不够大，能不能说我在拿命冒险？你知道，我只有9%的死亡概率，而我至少需要13%的概率。他太逗了。两年前他问我这些东西时也是这个样子。我当时就说，哥们，怎么最合理就怎么做。是啊。我是说，显然，我觉得我的直觉不太靠谱。但我意识到的是，我不必相信自己的直觉。

cues.en: This problem of getting the best title and thumbnail, it's a scientific problem.
cues.zh: 想选出最佳标题和缩略图，这其实是个科学问题。

cues.en: We're just asking which accurate representation of the video will get the most clicks from a general audience, and that's a problem we can use the scientific method to solve.
cues.zh: 我们要问的是，哪种对视频的准确呈现能赢得大众最多的点击，而这个问题可以用科学方法来解决。

cues.en: So I've hired a couple of really bright people and we spend a lot of time brainstorming
cues.zh: 所以我雇了几个非常聪明的人，我们花大量时间头脑风暴，

cues.en: and making titles and thumbnails and testing them out. For example, on Twitter and Patreon.
cues.zh: 制作标题和缩略图并做测试。比如在Twitter和Patreon上测试。

cues.en: Veritasium titles and thumbnails have gotten better not because I'm better at it, but because of my team and our testing.
cues.zh: Veritasium的标题和缩略图越来越好，不是因为我更在行了，而是因为我的团队和我们的测试。

cues.en: If you have ideas about how we could do it better, please get in touch. The results have often contradicted what I expected. I mean, this video seemed to perform 10% better when we excluded the word surprising from the title, so it became simply The Secret of Synchronization.
cues.zh: 如果你有更好的做法，请联系我们。结果常常和我的预期相反。比如这个视频，当我们把“surprising”一词从标题中去掉后，表现好了10%，于是标题就变成了简单的《The Secret of Synchronization》。

cues.en: I thought these two titles were basically a toss-up, but Patreon had a strong preference for one over the other. What's interesting about this research is that the more clickable titles and thumbnails often better represent the content of the video. Let me give you some examples. You know, one thing I didn't expect when YouTube brought in the real time analytics tools and allowed title and thumbnail changes to affect impressions
cues.zh: 我原以为这两个标题基本不相上下，但Patreon上用户对其中一个的偏好明显更强。这项研究有趣的地方在于，更吸引点击的标题和缩略图往往能更好地呈现视频内容。我举几个例子。你知道吗，有件事我没料到，就是当YouTube推出实时分析工具、并允许修改标题和缩略图来影响展示量时，

cues.en: was that it would also work for older videos.
cues.zh: 它居然对老视频也有效。

cues.en: So here is an old video that I originally entitled why the neutron is the hero of nuclear physics.
cues.zh: 所以这是一段老视频，我最初给它起的标题是《为什么中子是核物理的英雄》。

cues.en: In hindsight, it's a weird kinda meaningless title. So, I changed it to why Einstein thought nuclear weapons impossible.
cues.zh: 事后看，这个标题有点奇怪，也没什么意义。所以我把它改成了《为什么爱因斯坦认为核武器不可能》。

cues.en: It's clearer, more accurate,
cues.zh: 它更清楚，也更准确，

cues.en: and this is what happened to views after the change.
cues.zh: 而这是改完之后播放量的变化。

cues.en: I changed strange applications of the Magnus effect to backspin basketball flies off dam. Again, more accurate and the video is now being watched on YouTube.
cues.zh: 我把《马格努斯效应的奇怪应用》改成了《后旋篮球飞出大坝》。同样更准确，现在这个视频正在 YouTube 上被观看。

cues.en: Probably 10,000,000 more views than it otherwise would have had. Even anti clickbait has proven effective. Here's a video I originally titled, are negative ions good for you? Which is a question nobody asked ever.
cues.zh: 大概比原本多了 1000 万播放量。连反标题党都被证明有效。这里有个视频，我原本标题是《负离子对你有好处吗？》——一个从来没人问过的问题。

cues.en: Now, I changed it to, do salt lamps work?
cues.zh: 后来我把它改成《盐灯有用吗？》

cues.en: Seriously.
cues.zh: 说真的。

cues.en: And here's the result.
cues.zh: 结果就是这样。

cues.en: One and a half million more views.
cues.zh: 多了一百五十万播放量。

cues.en: I think looking at these examples, could easily make the case that YouTube has made me better at what I do. It has improved the clarity and accuracy of my titles and thumbnails. It's helped me figure out what is interesting to my audience and how to encapsulate that in a single image in fewer than 50 characters.
cues.zh: 我觉得看这些例子，很容易证明 YouTube 让我更擅长自己的工作了。它让我的标题和缩略图更清晰、更准确。也帮我弄明白观众觉得什么有意思，以及如何用一张图和不到 50 个字符把它概括出来。

cues.en: For those of you who worry that a focus on titles and thumbnails will prevent me from picking challenging science topics, well, I simply ask you to look at the videos from the last year or two, like the ones on Goodell's incompleteness theorem, general relativity, Penrose tilings, the logistic map, Newton's method of calculating pi, the one way speed of light.
cues.zh: 如果你担心关注标题和缩略图会让我不再选有挑战性的科学话题，那我只需请你看看过去一两年的视频，比如关于哥德尔不完备定理、广义相对论、彭罗斯密铺、逻辑斯蒂映射、牛顿计算圆周率的方法、单向光速的那些。

cues.en: Good titles and thumbnails make it possible to tackle these topics and to reach more people who have never heard of them before.
cues.zh: 好的标题和封面让我们能挑战这些选题，并触及更多以前从未听过它们的人。

cues.en: There is a symbiotic relationship between views and video quality. The more views we get, the more people, locations,
cues.zh: 播放量和视频质量之间存在一种共生关系。播放量越高，我们就能投入越多人力、场地、

cues.en: props, and equipment, and research we can invest in.
cues.zh: 道具、设备以及研究资源。

cues.en: This makes the next video better than the last.
cues.zh: 这让下一期视频总能比上一期做得更好。

cues.en: If we can be good at titles and thumbnails, the ultimate outcome is better videos.
cues.zh: 如果我们能把标题和封面做好，最终的结果就是产出更优质的视频。

cues.en: That is something I think you and I both want.
cues.zh: 我想这正是你我都希望看到的。
